newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu slips gently to 3,300/10 vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu slips gently to 3,300/10 vs dlr.

text.p: Romania's leu closed Wednesday only slightly weaker at 3,300/10 to the dollar against a previous 3,295/3,305 on a forex market unmoved by a grim forecast of its imminent plunge.

Bancorex's First Vice-President Alexandru Ghiba told the newspaper Adevarul that the leu was vastly overvalued and would fall sharply after the November 3 general elections. He said the true value of the leu was closer to 5,500 to 6,000 and put it at between 10,000 and 12,000 within a year.
The government and the central bank dismissed the notion out of hand.
Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu, speaking to Reuters in London, said the leu should ease to 3,400-3,500. Finance Minister Florin Georgescu said Ghiba's forecast was unrealistic.
Most forex traders said the leu was unlikely to see a sharp fall immediately, although its current level was too high and predicted growing import-led dollar buying orders.

"We are waiting for a leu slide because pressure on it generally grows in the winter. It has been artificially high for months but that estimate goes too far," said a trader with one of the four market-making dealer banks.
Operators said the leu's real range was up to 4,500 to the dollar and some of them said the leu would not easily breach the 4,000 level by the end of the year.

Most deals on the forex market, battered by distortions and sharp changes in rules, are struck in other currencies, which at cross yield leu-dollar prices near the 3,570 level offered by retail currency shops.
Short-term money market rates eased towards 44 percent from some 45-46 percent in early trading, dealers said. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
